name: WeWF World Championship
epitaph: The belt passed through fourteen recorded reigns and ten men between January 1991 and March 1992 — Volcano and Juggernaut inside one turn, then the General four separate times, Frank Steel, DiMadMan, the Big Kahuna, Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel” and “Irish” Mike Flint inside a single week in May, and Mr. Roddy, Steelgrave, the Sandman and Metal after it.

name: WeWF Americas Championship
epitaph: One of three Continental belts. It changed hands seven times in fourteen weeks, was declared vacant when Frank Steel found himself holding three belts at once, was settled in an eight-man tournament, and ended on a Boston crab at a Supercard — after which the Summer League simply did not carry it.

name: WeWF Eurasia Championship
epitaph: One of three Continental belts, held in turn by the Lethal Lemming, “Irish” Mike Flint twice, Destruction, AquaDemon, BudMan and the Millionaire; the last of those won it eight days before the league downsized for the summer and never defended it.

name: WeWF Africa/Australia Championship
epitaph: One of three Continental belts, and the only one whose reigns the reports date almost end to end: the Crusher, the General, Mr. Roddy, Tom “the Animal” Brown, DiMadMan twice and WindWarrior, before DiMadMan vacated it on winning the World Championship and Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel” won the tournament that filled it across three nights of one turn.

name: WeWF Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Thirteen recorded reigns and eight teams in thirteen months: the Dynamic Machine, the Leaping Lords, the Maniacs, Flint and Steel three times, the Intoxicators, the Law three times, the Highlanders, the Hoosiers twice and RnR — the Law's own third win in February 1992 counted on air, and this ledger's count of their reigns matches the broadcast's exactly.

name: TWIW TV Championship
epitaph: The newsdesk's own singles belt, wrestled for across federation lines: Mr. B held it into 1992 and kept it on a disqualification he was himself the subject of, the Hangman of the IWF took it from him with his own noose on 15 February, and defended it against the UeWF, the WeWF and a bout the championship committee annulled.

name: TWIW TV Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Created by the newsdesk in March 1992 and settled in a four-round, eight-team tournament drawn from four federations; the Annihilation Alliance won the final over the WeWF's own tag champions with the loser unconscious on the floor from a blowgun dart.

name: WeWF United States Championship
epitaph: Created for the 1991 Summer League and settled in one night: a sixteen-man tournament in which Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel” beat BudMan in an all-Four-Corners final, cleanly enough that both announcers remarked on it — and then held the belt undefeated through five defenses.

name: WeWF Six-Man Championship
epitaph: A three-man belt that appears in the record already held: three masked men calling themselves Apocalypse Now beat the Superstars for it in the league's fifteenth turn, and the Down-Under Decking Crew took it off them in the twenty-second — after which the newsdesk's own last word is that the titles were retired and two-thirds of the belts are still in Devastation, Inc.'s hands, because the man who holds the third would not give it up.

name: The WeWF Battle Royal
epitaph: The battle royals the WeWF staged in 1991, each with its own winner: the league's first, for $100,000 from Mr. Fujikuchi's Akira Foundation; the Team Challenge Series battle royal; and a sixteen-team Tag Team Battle Royal.

name: The WeWF Iron Man Trophy
epitaph: The trophy of the WeWF's Iron Man Tournament. The Big Kahuna won the first, at the Supercard of 30 April 1991, beating the Romulan Mauler in the final round, and kept it in a four-man round robin at the August Supercard, unbeaten at 3-0.
